newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian funds grew thanks to equities.
newsitem.headline: Belgian funds grew thanks to equities.

text.p: Investment funds sold in Belgium managed 2,636.1 billion Belgian francs ($70.1 billion) in assets at the end of June, up 25 percent on the year-earlier period, the Belgian Investment Fund Association said on Wednesday.
Assets under management at end-June were up 10 percent from 2,397.5 billions at end-March, the Association said.
The figures include funds sold by domestic and foreign institutions.

Growth was strongest in capital guaranteed funds whose return is linked to stock market indices. The value of assets under management by these so-called "click funds" was 286.0 billion francs, up from 207.6 billion at the end of March and 111.2 billion francs one year ago.
Traditional equity-linked funds assets rose to 379.6 billion francs from 307.5 billion at end March and 243.7 billion last year.
Assets under management by long-term (over three years) bond funds were 1,075.5 billion francs, up from 1,018.7 billion at the end of March and 912.8 billion one year ago.
Money market and short-term bond funds saw their share of assets fall to respectively 275.8 and 92.9 billion francs.
